# Gains: Get all gains for an account

Area overview and notes: [gains.md](../gains.md)

`GET /gains` · tenant-scoped token

A detailed collection of all combined cost bases, proceeds, and gains/losses. These correspond to line items on an IRS form 8949 or form 1099-B.

**Query parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `account_id` | string | No | Your system's unique identifier for the Account. |
| `client_disposition_transaction_id` | string | No | The customer transaction ID of a disposing transaction, used to retrieve a specific set of gains. You can specify up to 25 client_disposition_transaction_id parameters to retrieve gains for multiple transactions. |
| `continuation_key` | string | No | A token used to indicate when to resume pagination of results. This is provided by the API in response to a previous request. |
| `end_date` | string (date-time) | No | ISO-8601 formatted date as a filter end date. |
| `page_size` | integer | No | The number of gains to include in each page of results returned by the API. |
| `start_date` | string (date-time) | No | ISO-8601 formatted date as a filter start date. |

**Headers**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x-user-id` | string (uuid) | No | The Taxbit UUID of the account. Ignored if account_id is specified. |

| `data[].gain_type` | string | Yes | Holding-period classification. Standard disposition methods return "long-term" (disposed lot held for more than one year) or "short-term" (one year or less, or missing cost basis). Accounts using the AUSTRIA disposition method instead return the inventory pool the disposal drew from: "at-new-stock" (Known Cost Basis), "at-user-basis" (User-Basis Stock), "at-missing-basis" (50% rule), "at-old-stock-long-term" or "at-old-stock-short-term" (Old Stock, excluded from withholding). A single disposal can emit one row per pool. One of: `long-term`, `short-term`, `at-new-stock`, `at-user-basis`, `at-missing-basis`, `at-old-stock-long-term`, `at-old-stock-short-term`. |
